title: Memory heatmap calibration for long-context Llama/Mistral/Qwen variants
creator: Aisha Raman
description:
Problem statement: For 32k+ token workloads we are seeing inconsistent memory headroom across model families (Llama-extended, Mistral-LongCtx, Qwen-32K). Current slab allocators and KV residency heuristics cause high fragmentation in some model variants and over-allocation in others. This results in lower batch packing efficiency and increased VM/host memory pressure during tail requests.

Goal: Build a repeatable calibration workflow ("heatmap calibration") that produces model-specific memory tuning artifacts: per-layer slab targets, KV slice priorities, preferred eviction buckets, and batch-shaping parameters. These artifacts should be small JSON/YAML configs the runtime can load to optimize allocation and eviction for a given model variant + long-context profile.

Approach and scope:
- Data collection: run a set of representative long-context traces (synthetic and customer-supplied prompts) through recent model variants (llama-70b-longctx, mistral-40b-extended, qwen-32k) with continuous batching enabled. Collect per-step GPU allocation maps, slab usage histograms, KV hit/residency, kernel launch profiles, and host spill events.
- Heatmap generation: convert the time-series into per-layer 'temperature' maps (hot = high residency/alloc churn). Identify persistent hot layers, transient streaming hot-spots (prefix-heavy), and cold tails.
- Calibration engine: produce tuning artifacts that change three runtime knobs: slab target sizes (per-device/per-variant), KV slice admission priorities (short-lived vs persistent), and batch shaping thresholds (max-concurrent-requests per model shard). Also include optional conservative host-spill policies for Qwen when memory pressure is severe.
- Validation: run a calibration validation job that compares baseline vs tuned on p50/p95 latency, tail OOM rate, throughput (tokens/s), and allocation fragmentation metric. Record the heatmap before/after and generate a diff.

Trade-offs considered:
- Aggressive compaction reduces fragmentation but increases CPU compaction cost and may increase p95 latency during compaction windows. We bias towards slight compaction during low-util windows.
- Increasing KV slice admission for prefix-heavy workloads improves latency for hot-prefix customers but reduces batch packing for cold workloads; the calibration engine will emit policies keyed by traffic pattern labels.
- Host spill fallback for Qwen reduces OOMs but adds >2x token-latency on spilled tokens; this is a last-resort policy only applied when safe-fallover is configured for the deployment.

Deliverables:
- calibration-runner tool (python) that creates per-model heatmaps and outputs tuning artifacts (yaml).
- set of tuned artifacts for the three target variants in a format the runtime can consume.
- retrofitted unit / integration tests and a CI job to run a lightweight calibration on nightly builds.
- results doc (Confluence) and a Grafana dashboard showing before/after metrics.

Risks and mitigations:
- Calibration overfitting to synthetic traces: mitigate by requiring at least one real-customer trace or a diversified synthetic suite per run.
- Complexity of runtime knobs: define a clear config schema with sensible defaults and a "safe mode" fallback.
- Upgrade compatibility: provide a migration script and runtime schema versioning so older deployments ignore unknown knobs.
acceptance_criteria: Calibration runner ingests traces and produces a heatmap artifact for each model variant
Tuning artifacts loadable by runtime without crashing (schema validation in CI)
Validated improvement: >=10% reduction in allocation fragmentation metric and no regression >5% p95 latency in standard throughput tests
Artifacts published to /infra/configs/memory-calibrations/{model_variant} with changelog and author
Nightly calibration smoke job runs in CI and fails if the schema validation or basic perf checks regress
comments: 2025-09-16 - Initial spike: Aisha created the runner prototype that captures per-layer alloc maps using CUPTI traces and a lightweight agent. Prototype repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/memory-heatmap-runner (WIP)

2025-09-20 - Data collection: Marco ran synthetic 32k traces for llama-70b-longctx and observed two persistent hotspots in layers 34-37 across 3 different seeds. Mistral had a more uniform spread but higher transient churn at early layers.

2025-09-22 - Decision: For Llama variants we will bias slab growth on the mid transformer block range; for Mistral we prefer smaller uniform slabs and higher KV slice admission. Qwen will default to conservative host-spill thresholds. Recorded in design notes: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Heatmap+Calibration+Notes
2025-09-26 - PR opened for calibration runner and yaml artifact writer: https://github.com/redwood-inference/memory-heatmap-runner/pull/12 — request review from @elenam and @ryan

2025-09-29 - Validation run v1: baseline vs tuned on a 4-GPU p4d-like cluster. Results: fragmentation metric down 13%, p50 steady, p95 +3% (within acceptance but flagged for follow-up). Throughput (tokens/s) increased 7% during steady state batching windows.

2025-10-01 - Review feedback from Ryan: tighten compaction windows to avoid p95 blips during bursty arrival patterns. Marco updated runner to create compaction windows during low load periods. New config samples added to artifact set.

2025-10-02 - Next: run customer trace validation for two pilot customers and schedule a canary rollout in dedicated for runtime-1.22. Dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/abc123/heatmap-calibration (internal)
